title: SegScope: Probing Fine-grained Interrupts via Architectural Footprints
problem: Existing countermeasures against interrupt-based side-channel attacks focus on disabling timers and removing file interface access, but do not address architectural footprints from segment protection mechanisms. Data segment register values observable during interrupts on x86 CPUs create an unexploited side-channel vector.
motivation: Interrupts are critical OS kernel resources that can be exploited for keylogging, website inference, GPU detection, and process fingerprinting; identifying new attack vectors beyond timer-based approaches is essential for security.
method: SegScope exploits x86 segment protection by observing that data segment register values leave detectable footprints when interrupts occur. The technique captures these architectural footprints to probe interrupts at fine granularity without requiring any timer mechanism, working across Intel and AMD CPUs where segment protection is widely deployed.
key_novelty: Using segment protection architectural footprints (data segment register values) as a side-channel vector to observe interrupts without any timer mechanism.
contributions: Novel interrupt-probing technique exploiting segment protection footprints instead of timers, working across Intel and AMD x86 processors
Practical attacks demonstrating website inference (92.4% Chrome, 87.4% Tor), cryptographic key extraction from CIRCL, and DNN model architecture theft (80% accuracy)
Noise reduction achieving 56× error rate improvement for other side-channel attacks like Spectral
Fine-grained timer construction from interrupt timestamps achieving rdtsc-level granularity, enabling KASLR breaks in 10 seconds and Flush+Reload Spectre attacks
